run.answer: NEAT (non-exercise activity thermogenesis) — это энергия, которую вы сжигаете в процессе обычной повседневной деятельности вне структурированных упражнений: ходьба, ерзанье, домашние дела, подъем по лестнице, ходьба из стороны в сторону, стояние и общая ежедневная активность [1]. Во время диеты уровень NEAT может снижаться незаметно для человека: вы можете больше сидеть, меньше двигаться или подсознательно избегать усилий из-за снижения уровня энергии [1]. Это сокращение может уменьшить ваш дефицит калорий, даже если потребление пищи остается в рамках плана [1].

For heavy strength work, it is common and often useful to rest between two to five minutes between demanding sets [1]. Regarding session order, you should place the movement you care about most early in the session [1].
sources: 05-strength-programming-basics.md > Strength Programming Basics > Rest periods and session order

run.answer: Weekly volume is likely appropriate if you experience steady progress in load or reps, soreness that fades between sessions, stable technique on later sets, and the target muscle feels challenged [1]. Conversely, if performance falls and soreness lingers throughout the week, the volume may be too high for your current context [1].
sources: 06-hypertrophy-training.md > Hypertrophy Training > Sets per week and dosing volume

run.answer: Red flags for accumulated fatigue or overtraining include a persistent drop in performance across multiple sessions, unusual fatigue that rest days do not fix, and sleep disruption despite feeling exhausted [1]. Other signs include frequent minor illness, low mood, flat motivation, unusual anxiety about training, an elevated resting heart rate, or a sense that recovery is lagging week after week [1].
sources: 07-sleep-and-recovery.md > Sleep and Recovery for Training Progress > Hard Training, Overreaching, and Overtraining

run.answer:
A practical shortlist for many recreational lifters includes [1]:
- creatine monohydrate (if strength or muscle gain is a priority and no contraindications exist) [1]
- caffeine (if tolerated and timed intelligently) [1]
- protein powder (if it helps meet protein intake goals) [1]
- vitamin D (only when personal context or clinical guidance supports it) [1]

Regarding vitamin D, it is an important health nutrient but not a universal supplement that everyone should take automatically [2]. The evidence-informed approach is to prioritize context; if deficiency is suspected, testing and clinical guidance can determine if supplementation is appropriate and what dose to use [2]. Because it is fat-soluble, casual megadosing is considered a poor strategy [2].

run.answer: A smart return to training follows a five-step logic: [1] first, calm the irritated tissue by reducing aggravating load; [1] second, maintain what you can train safely; [1] third, rebuild local strength and tolerance; [1] fourth, reintroduce sport- or lift-specific loading gradually; and [1] finally, progress based on symptom response, not ego.
sources: 11-injury-prevention-and-rehab.md > Injury Prevention and Rehab for People Who Train > Return to Training: Modify, Do Not Guess

run.answer: To reduce conflict when strength is your main goal, you should prioritize the quality of sessions that matter most to your goal [1]. It is recommended to use zone 2 modalities with low eccentric stress, such as cycling or incline walking, as these often fit better than frequent hard runs [1]. Additionally, you should keep most cardio easy, separate hard cardio and hard lifting when possible, and fuel appropriately, especially with carbohydrates around demanding work [1].
sources: 12-cardio-and-conditioning.md > Cardio and Conditioning for Strength, Health, and Work Capacity > Concurrent Training: Mixing Cardio and Strength

run.answer: Instead of chasing a flawless position, you should aim for support and variability [1]. Rather than trying to freeze in one shape, use training to increase tolerance [1]. Practical advice includes alternating between upright and relaxed positions, standing up, walking, or changing posture regularly [1]. Additionally, rows, carries, split squats, pressing with good trunk control, and general physical activity often help more than constantly trying to pin the shoulders back [1].
sources: 15-core-training-and-posture.md > Core Training, Bracing, and Posture Without the Myths > Better advice for desk workers

run.answer: A useful rule is to "never miss twice when it is avoidable" [1]. Instead of self-criticism or trying to make up every missed workout, which can create an exhausting backlog, the best follow-up action is to return to your normal schedule and keep momentum [1].
sources: 16-motivation-habits-and-consistency.md > Motivation, Habits, and Consistency in Fitness > Dealing with missed sessions

- at least one vertical pull [1]
- at least one row [1]
- some rear-delt or face-pull work [1]
- enough total volume to progress without inflaming the elbows [1]

run.answer: The distinction between high-bar and low-bar positioning is based on where the bar rests on the body and its effect on posture: in a high-bar position, the bar rests on the upper traps, which typically allows for a more upright torso and increased knee travel [1]. In contrast, the low-bar position places the bar lower across the rear delts, which often allows for more load but requires a firmer upper-back shelf and typically involves more torso lean [2].

run.answer: Если тренировки частые или требовательные, время приема пищи имеет значение [1]. До тренировки рекомендуется съесть порцию, содержащую углеводы и немного белка, за один-три часа до начала [1]. После тренировки не обязательно есть немедленно; разумно употребить белок и немного углеводов в течение нескольких часов после занятия, особенно если следующий прием пищи будет нескоро [1].

run.answer: Если вы столкнулись с плато, сначала проверьте следующее: была ли соблюдена приверженность диете [1], действительно ли средний вес стоит на месте в течение нескольких недель [1], не снизилась ли активность вне тренировок [1], и нет ли причин для задержки воды (например, стресс, тяжелые тренировки, запор, высокое потребление натрия или гормональные сдвиги) [1]. Если плато реально, рекомендуемые правки включают: небольшое снижение калорийности [1], увеличение ежедневной активности [1], повышение точности порций [1] и улучшение стабильности в выходные дни [1]. Резкое сокращение еды требуется редко [1].
sources: 09-fat-loss-and-body-composition.md > Fat Loss and Body Composition Without Losing the Plot > Tracking Intake and Progress > Measurements and photos

- Вариация становой тяги (Deadlift variation): 3 подхода по 5–6 повторений [1].
- Фронтальные, кубковые или хак-приседания (Front squat, goblet squat, or hack squat): 3 подхода по 8–10 повторений [1].

- Степ-ап или выпады при ходьбе (Step-up or walking lunge): 2 подхода на каждую сторону [1].
- Упражнение Паллофа или переноска (Pallof press or carry): 2–3 подхода [1].

run.answer: Для прогресса без травм новичкам рекомендуется придерживаться следующих правил: использовать интервалы бега и ходьбы [1], постепенно увеличивать общий объем [1], держать большинство пробежек в легком темпе [1], выбирать удобную обувь [1] и избегать ошибки превращения каждой пробежки в проверку возможностей [1]. Важно помнить, что ткани нуждаются во времени для адаптации к ударной нагрузке [1], а новички часто получают травмы, когда одновременно увеличивают дистанцию и интенсивность [1].

run.answer: Полезными признаками того, что восстановление проходит успешно, являются: [1] стабильные или улучшающиеся показатели при тех же усилиях, [1] мышечная боль, которая проходит во время разминки, [1] нормальная мотивация к тренировкам, [1] стабильный аппетит и настроение, [1] частота сердечных сокращений в покое остается в привычном диапазоне, а также [1] сон, который приносит чувство бодрости, а не просто достаточную продолжительность.

run.answer: Zone 2 is a relatively easy, sustainable intensity where you can still speak in short sentences and continue for a meaningful duration [2]. It should feel controlled rather than heroic [2], and easy aerobic work should feel sustainable and controlled [1]. Example modalities include brisk incline walking, easy jogging, steady cycling, rowing at a controlled pace, and elliptical work that stays conversational [2]. The provided text does not specify an exact heart-rate percentage to target on a watch, noting instead that heart-rate zones are estimates and it is better to combine them with perceived effort [1].
sources: 12-cardio-and-conditioning.md > Cardio and Conditioning for Strength, Health, and Work Capacity > Heart-Rate Zones: Useful, Not Sacred

For heavy strength work, it is common and often useful to rest between two to five minutes between demanding sets [1]. Regarding session order, you should place the movement you care about most early in the session [1].
sources: 05-strength-programming-basics.md > Strength Programming Basics > Rest periods and session order

run.answer: Weekly volume is likely appropriate if you experience steady progress in load or reps, soreness that fades between sessions, stable technique on later sets, and the target muscle feels challenged [1]. Conversely, if performance falls and soreness lingers throughout the week, the volume may be too high for your current context [1].
sources: 06-hypertrophy-training.md > Hypertrophy Training > Sets per week and dosing volume

run.answer: Red flags for accumulated fatigue or overtraining include a persistent drop in performance across multiple sessions, unusual fatigue that rest days do not fix, and sleep disruption despite feeling exhausted [1]. Other signs include frequent minor illness, low mood, flat motivation, unusual anxiety about training, an elevated resting heart rate, or a sense that recovery is lagging week after week [1].
sources: 07-sleep-and-recovery.md > Sleep and Recovery for Training Progress > Hard Training, Overreaching, and Overtraining

run.answer:
A practical shortlist for many recreational lifters includes [1]:
- creatine monohydrate (if strength or muscle gain is a priority and no contraindications exist) [1]
- caffeine (if tolerated and timed intelligently) [1]
- protein powder (if it helps meet protein intake goals) [1]
- vitamin D (only when personal context or clinical guidance supports it) [1]

Regarding vitamin D, it is an important health nutrient but not a universal supplement that everyone should take automatically [2]. The evidence-informed approach is to prioritize context; if deficiency is suspected or known, testing and clinical guidance can determine if supplementation is appropriate and what dose to use [2]. Because it is fat-soluble, casual megadosing is considered a poor strategy [2].

run.answer: A smart return to training follows a five-step logic: [1] first, calm the irritated tissue by reducing aggravating load; [2] maintain what you can train safely; [3] rebuild local strength and tolerance; [4] reintroduce sport- or lift-specific loading gradually; and [5] progress based on symptom response, rather than ego [1].
sources: 11-injury-prevention-and-rehab.md > Injury Prevention and Rehab for People Who Train > Return to Training: Modify, Do Not Guess

run.answer: To reduce conflict when strength is your main goal, you should prioritize the quality of sessions that matter most to your goal [1]. It is recommended to use zone 2 modalities with low eccentric stress, such as cycling or incline walking, as these often fit better than frequent hard runs [1]. Additionally, you should keep most cardio easy, separate hard cardio and hard lifting when possible, and fuel appropriately, especially with carbohydrates around demanding work [1].
sources: 12-cardio-and-conditioning.md > Cardio and Conditioning for Strength, Health, and Work Capacity > Concurrent Training: Mixing Cardio and Strength

run.answer: Instead of chasing a flawless position, you should aim for support and variability [1]. Rather than trying to freeze in one shape, use training to increase tolerance [1]. Practical advice includes alternating between upright and relaxed positions, standing up, walking, or changing posture regularly [1]. Additionally, rows, carries, split squats, pressing with good trunk control, and general physical activity often help more than constantly trying to pin the shoulders back [1].

run.answer: A useful rule is to "never miss twice when it is avoidable" [1]. Instead of self-criticism or trying to make up every missed workout, which can create an exhausting backlog, the best follow-up action is to return to your normal schedule and keep momentum [1].

run.answer: The distinction between high-bar and low-bar positioning is based on where the bar rests on the body and its effect on posture: in a high-bar position, the bar rests on the upper traps, which typically allows for a more upright torso and increased knee travel [1]. In contrast, the low-bar position places the bar lower across the rear delts, which often allows for more load but requires a firmer upper-back shelf and typically involves more torso lean [2].

run.answer: Если тренировки частые или требовательные, время приема пищи имеет значение [1]. До тренировки рекомендуется съесть порцию, содержащую углеводы и немного белка, за один-три часа до начала [1]. После тренировки не обязательно есть немедленно; разумно употребить белок и немного углеводов в течение нескольких часов после занятия, особенно если следующий прием пищи будет нескоро [1].

run.answer: Если вы столкнулись с плато, сначала проверьте следующее: была ли соблюдена приверженность диете [1], действительно ли средний вес стоит на месте в течение нескольких недель [1], не снизилась ли активность вне тренировок [1], и нет ли причин для задержки воды (например, стресс, тяжелые тренировки, запор, высокое потребление натрия или гормональные сдвиги) [1]. Если плато реально, рекомендуемые правки включают: небольшое снижение калорийности [1], увеличение ежедневной активности [1], повышение точности порций [1] и улучшение стабильности в выходные дни [1]. Резкое сокращение еды требуется редко [1].

В 4-дневном сплите для новичков (Lower B) входят следующие упражнения и диапазоны:

run.answer: Для прогресса без травм новичкам рекомендуется придерживаться следующих правил: использовать интервалы бега и ходьбы [1], постепенно увеличивать общий объем [1], держать большинство пробежек в легком темпе [1], выбирать удобную обувь [1] и избегать ошибки превращения каждой пробежки в проверку возможностей [1]. Важно помнить, что ткани нуждаются во времени для адаптации к ударной нагрузке [1], а новички часто получают травмы, когда одновременно увеличивают дистанцию и интенсивность [1].

run.answer: Полезными признаками того, что восстановление проходит успешно, являются: [1] стабильные или улучшающиеся показатели при тех же усилиях, [1] мышечная боль, которая проходит во время разминки, [1] нормальная мотивация к тренировкам, [1] стабильный аппетит и настроение, [1] частота сердечных сокращений в покое остается в привычном диапазоне, а также [1] сон, который приносит чувство бодрости, а не просто достаточную продолжительность.

run.answer: Zone 2 is a relatively easy, sustainable intensity where you can still speak in short sentences and continue for a meaningful duration [2]. It should feel controlled rather than heroic [2], and easy aerobic work should feel sustainable and controlled [1]. Example modalities include brisk incline walking, easy jogging, steady cycling, rowing at a controlled pace, and elliptical work that stays conversational [2]. The provided text does not specify an exact heart-rate percentage to target on a watch, noting instead that heart-rate zones are estimates and it is better to combine them with perceived effort [1].
